citation: Spitzer, R. L., Kroenke, K., Williams, J. B. W., & Löwe, B. (2006). A brief measure for assessing generalized anxiety disorder: The GAD-7. Archives of Internal Medicine, 166(10), 1092-1097.
description: A seven-item screen for the severity of anxiety symptoms over the last two weeks.

bands.description: Minimal anxiety symptoms. No action is needed on this screen alone.
bands.label: Minimal

bands.description: Mild anxiety symptoms. Talk to a doctor or a mental health professional if the symptoms last.
bands.label: Mild

bands.description: Moderate anxiety symptoms. This range is a reason to talk to a doctor or a mental health professional.
bands.label: Moderate

bands.description: Severe anxiety symptoms. Seek an assessment from a doctor or a mental health professional, and call a crisis line if you are in danger.
bands.label: Severe

domains.description: How severe the anxiety symptoms are, summed over the seven items.
domains.high: A higher score means more of the symptoms in the last two weeks.
domains.low: A lower score means fewer of the symptoms in the last two weeks.
domains.name: Anxiety severity

evidence.limitations: This is a screen, not a diagnosis. It records how you describe the last two weeks, so it can change from week to week. A clinician makes a diagnosis, and only with more information than a questionnaire.

validity.summary: A score of 10 or more detects generalised anxiety disorder with a sensitivity of 89 percent and a specificity of 82 percent in the development sample.

info.audience: Adults who want a short, structured look at how they have been feeling.
info.authors: Robert L. Spitzer, Kurt Kroenke, Janet B. W. Williams, and Bernd Löwe
notFor: A screen for every mental health concern.
info.responseScale: A four-point frequency scale, from Not at all to Nearly every day.
whatYouGet: The published severity band for that score.
A link that shares your result and a file that saves it.

instructions: Over the last two weeks, how often have you been bothered by each of the following problems? Answer for how you have actually been, not how you would like to be.

items.text: Feeling nervous, anxious, or on edge.
Not being able to stop or control worrying.
Worrying too much about different things.
Being so restless that it is hard to sit still.
Feeling afraid, as if something awful might happen.
